\looseness=-1 The key finding is that \emph{gating}, not correction strength, is the mechanism. CRM always-on applies the same learned residual to every step, including the ${\sim}$80--90\% where the VLA is already confident; corrections on these steps are noise that averages out any benefit. ACR-VLA's adaptive gate triggers CRM only on high-uncertainty steps (trigger rate 4--20\%, varying with suite difficulty), preserving the VLA's own output elsewhere. ACR-VLA's adaptive gate triggers correction only on high-uncertainty steps (4--20\% of steps), maintaining baseline on confident suites while avoiding this degradation. $K{=}10$ argmin selection~\cite{chen2026reconvla} hurts on Goal ($-$2.9\,pp); selection without learned correction is insufficient. ACR-VLA uses $5{\times}$ fewer VLA forward passes than the $K{=}10$ methods. A boundary analysis on OpenVLA-OFT~\cite{kim2024openvla} (7B, deterministic $L_1$ regression), where $97.3$\% of steps produce near-identical actions, confirms that stochastic diversity is a prerequisite.

\looseness=-1 The key finding is mechanistic: \emph{when} to correct matters more than correction strength. CRM always-on applies the same learned residual to every step, including the ${\sim}$80--90\% where the VLA is already confident; corrections on these steps are noise. ACR-VLA's adaptive gate triggers CRM only on high-uncertainty steps (trigger rate 4--20\%, varying with suite difficulty), preserving the VLA's own output elsewhere. Threshold sweeps on two suites confirm an inverted-U response: too much correction is as harmful as too little, establishing gating as a necessary safety mechanism.

1	We propose ACR-VLA, a lightweight test-time refinement pipeline for frozen flow-matching VLAs. A 327K-parameter Correction Residual Module (CRM) learns residual corrections from VLA observation features, while an adaptive gating mechanism uses $K{=}2$ pairwise action distance as a per-step uncertainty signal ($\rho{=}0.9979$ with ten-sample variance, zero additional latency) to selectively apply correction only when needed.       post-hoc correction (CRM always-on) helps on some tasks but actively
      degrades others (-1.2pp Object, -2.2pp Long).
    gap: >
      No mechanism to selectively apply learned corrections based on per-step
      VLA uncertainty. Existing methods (A2C2: temporal staleness, ReconVLA:
      UQ-only, SC-VLA: RL required) don't address adaptive inference-time
      correction allocation.
    insight: >
      WHEN to correct matters more than correction strength. K=2 pairwise L2
      is a near-perfect uncertainty proxy (ρ=0.9979 vs K=10 variance) at
      zero additional latency cost.
    mechanism: >
      Adaptive gate: d₂ > τ → CRM correction; d₂ ≤ τ → direct output.
      Trigger rate correlates monotonically with effect size.
    evidence: >
      Spatial +1.4pp (p<0.05, n=8 paired). Adaptive ≥ CRM always-on on ALL
